summary_paragraph: A man with a history of cocaine-induced cardiomyopathy, insulin-dependent diabetes, COPD, and chronic hepatitis C was admitted for acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation, triggered by poor adherence to fluid and sodium restrictions. He presented with weight gain, leg edema, and shortness of breath. Treatment included IV furosemide for diuresis, which successfully reduced his weight from 92.3 kg to 83.7 kg, improved respiratory symptoms, and resolved pulmonary edema. His kidney function improved from a creatinine of 2.2 to 1.8, and losartan was restarted and titrated to 25 mg daily. Insulin therapy was adjusted due to labile glucose levels, and he was discharged on glargine 30 units at bedtime. He was counseled on daily weight monitoring, low-salt diet, fluid restriction, and avoidance of cocaine and tobacco, with follow-up arranged.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Diabetes with other specified manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
